Address.description:
The address of an agent: a thread on a target.

On the wire this is an **opaque string**. Agents never construct one; they get it from a
tool result, a received message, or the user. Its three immutable parts are the target id
(not the renamable target name), the provider instance with its store binding, and the
native thread id; the last two are what [`ThreadId`] encodes. The format is
`<target id>/<thread id>`; a target id never contains `/`. Decoding never fails: a string
that does not have that shape is kept and simply has no parts.

AgreedProtocol.description: The daemon's range and the version agreed: the lower of the two maxima, if it is not below either minimum. Frozen core.

AppliedSettings.description: The model / effort / mode the harness reports it is **actually** using.

reason.description: A reason, when the decision accepts one.

acceptsReason.description: Whether the user may attach a reason ("deny with a reason").

ApprovalRequest.description: "May I run this / change these / have this permission?"

changes.description: The file changes, for a file-change approval.

command.description: The command, for a command approval.

cwd.description: The directory it would run in.

decisions.description: The decisions the harness actually offers.

details.description: Anything else the harness sent, for a generic rendering.

scope.description: The scope of the grant, for a permission approval.

BackendKind.description: The backend an instance actually runs on.

BackendPreference.description: The backend an instance is configured to use.

Capability.description: A flag the UI checks before offering a feature. Branch on these, never on provider kind.

ClientId.description:
A stable id for one host's YAAC client (the hub), sent in `initialize`, so `yaacd` can
say which client answered a request or drives a thread.

host.description: Host name, shown to other clients as "In use on …".

id.description: Stable id of this host's client, so `yaacd` can tell clients apart across reconnects.

ContextUsage.description: How full the context window is.

Control.description: Who may act on a thread, **from the point of view of the client receiving it**.

ControlChangedEvent.description: `controlChanged`: who may act on the thread changed (relative to the receiving client).

activeTurn.description: The running turn, when there is one (needed for Stop).

holder.description: Where it is in use, for the read-only states.

DaemonBusy.description: What the daemon is busy with.

DaemonHandoverParams.description: `daemon/handover` params. Frozen core; valid even after a failed negotiation; idempotent.

DaemonHandoverResult.description: `daemon/handover` result: sent before the daemon closes the connection. Frozen core.

DaemonInfo.description: The daemon's build and on-disk state format.

stateFormat.description: What is on disk. Separate from the protocol version.

DecisionKind.description:
The nature of a decision the harness offers. The UI renders the offered decisions; it
never assumes a fixed Allow/Deny pair.

DeltaField.description: The item field an `itemDelta` appends to.

DiagnosticSection.description: One section of a diagnostics report.

title.description: Section title (`daemon`, an instance's display name, …).

EffortId.description: An effort level, opaque and ordered as the harness reports it.

EffortInfo.description: An effort level a model offers.

description.description: Longer description, when the harness gives one.

displayName.description: Label to show; when absent, show the id.

Empty.description:
An empty JSON object, for methods that take or return nothing (`{}` on the wire).

Kept as an object rather than `null` so fields can be added later without a version bump.

Epoch.description: A journal epoch: one continuous journal. Changes only when a journal is started afresh.

ErrorCode.description:
A stable error code for the UI to branch on. Open: codes this build does not know are
kept, and the `message` is always shown as-is.

FileChange.description: One file in a file-change approval.

FilePart.description: An upload referenced by its path on the target; the agent reads it with its own tools.

values.description: Field values, shaped by the form's schema.

FormRequest.description:
A schema-driven form (MCP elicitation and the like). Until the UI renders forms it shows
`message` and says the form must be answered in the harness.

schema.description: JSON Schema of the requested fields, as the harness sent it.

source.description: Who asks (e.g. an MCP server name).

FsListParams.description: `fs/list`: list a directory on the target.

path.description: The directory; the user's home when absent.

parent.description: Its parent, when it has one.

HandoffItem.description: `handoff`: marks history a forked thread inherited from its parent.

cutoffTurn.description: The last turn of the source that was carried.

transcript.description:
The frozen transcript (markdown), for a handoff fork; rendered read-only above the
divider. Bounded like any item field.

transcriptPath.description: The transcript file on the target, in `yaacd`'s state directory.

HandoverState.description: What the daemon will do about a hand-over.

HandoverWhen.description: When the daemon should step aside.

ImagePart.description:
An upload given to the model as real image input. Only valid when the thread's effective
`imageInput` is not `unsupported`; `yaacd` rejects it with `capability_missing` otherwise.

protocol.description: The protocol versions the client speaks.
The daemon's range and the agreed version.

schemaHash.description:
Hash of the frozen baseline schema of the agreed version. A diagnostic: a mismatch
means one side has a wrong idea of what that version is.

InputPart.description: One part of a user message.

InstanceId.description: A provider instance on a target (`pi_01J…`). Stable, generated by `yaacd`.

Item.description:
One item of a turn: common fields plus the kind-specific body (flattened, so `kind` sits
next to `id` on the wire).

ItemDeltaEvent.description: `itemDelta`: text to append to one field of an item.

ItemEvent.description: `itemStarted` / `itemCompleted`: an item appeared, or reached a final state.

ItemUpdatedEvent.description:
`itemUpdated`: a full replacement snapshot of an item.

With `throughSeq`, this one event replaces every event from the envelope's `seq` through
`throughSeq` (journal compaction, or backpressure collapse); the client advances its
position to `throughSeq`.

throughSeq.description: The last sequence number this snapshot replaces.

JournalPosition.description: A position in a thread's journal.

ListModelsQuery.description: `listModels`: the instances on the destination and their models.

providers.description: The same live descriptors as the model picker.

MeshBudget.description: Allowance per orchestration root, counted across all targets.

agentTurns.description: Turns started by agents (not by a person).

wallClockSecs.description: Wall-clock seconds since a person last acted on the root.

MeshBudgetParams.description: `mesh/budget`: read or continue an orchestration's budget. Sent to the target of the root.

MeshBudgetPatch.description: A change to the budget. Absent fields are unchanged.

exhausted.description: Whether it has run out (messages are stored but not dispatched).

MeshBudgetUsage.description: How much of a budget is used.

wallClockSecs.description: Seconds since a person last acted on the root.

MeshDeliverParams.description:
`mesh/deliver` (hub → target): put a message into a recipient's mailbox. The target
answers once it is on disk. Retried by the hub until answered.

pairMessages.description: Messages between the same two threads per window.

runningThreads.description: Threads running at once on this target (a thread blocked in `wait` does not count).

undeliveredNoticeSecs.description: After this many seconds undelivered, the sender gets a notice.

MeshLimitsPatch.description: A change to some limits. Absent fields are unchanged.

MeshMessage.description:
A message between two agents. Sender and body are separate fields all the way to the
harness.

from.description:
Stamped by `yaacd` from the sender's attachment ticket, never by the agent. For a
`notice`, the thread the notice is about.

id.description: Unique; every hop deduplicates by it.

root.description: The orchestration root this message belongs to.

seq.description:
Position in the sender-to-recipient sequence (starts at 1). The recipient's dispatcher
hands messages over in this order.

MeshPeer.description: A readable label for another agent: "title · provider · target".

reachable.description: Whether its target is currently reachable. Absent: not known.

targetName.description: Target name, as the user named it.

MeshPolicy.description: The mesh policy of one target.

acceptFromOtherTargets.description: Whether agents on other targets may start or message threads here at all.

mode.description: Allow, ask first, or always ask.

MeshPolicyMode.description:
Whether spawning, cross-target sending, and reading outside one's orchestration happen
freely or ask the user first (with an ordinary request card).

MeshPolicyParams.description:
`mesh/policy`: read the policy, and change it when `update` is present (then `opId` is
required).

MeshPolicyUpdate.description:
A change to the policy. Absent fields are unchanged, so an older client never erases
settings it does not know.

MeshQuery.description: A tool call that needs another target.

MeshQueryParams.description:
`mesh/query`. Sent by the source `yaacd` to the hub with `target` = destination; the hub
forwards the same params to the destination `yaacd` and relays the answer back.

caller.description: The calling thread, stamped by its `yaacd`.

MeshQueryResult.description:
`mesh/query` result; its `tool` matches the query's. Failures are ordinary errors
(`target_offline`, `limit_exceeded`, `policy_denied`, …) with a readable message.

MeshReceiptParams.description:
`mesh/receipt` (hub → source target): a relayed message moved on (for example it reached
the recipient's mailbox after its target came back), so the sender's `meshSent` item can
be updated.

receipt.description: How far the message got, as far as the answering side knows.

MeshReceivedItem.description: `meshReceived`: a message this agent received. Never styled as a user message.

MeshRelayParams.description:
`mesh/relay` (target → hub): carry a message to another target. The hub answers once the
message is in its durable relay queue. Retried by the target until answered; the message id
makes a repeat harmless.

MeshRosterParams.description:
`mesh/roster` (hub → target): the target's own identity and the list of targets. Sent
after `initialize` and whenever it changes.

targets.description: Every target in the mesh, this one included.

receipt.description: How far it got. Updated (`itemUpdated`) as it moves.

childrenOf.description: Only threads spawned by this thread.

mine.description: Only threads in the caller's orchestration.

project.description: Only threads of this project (its cross-target key or path).

text.description: Free text matched against title and preview.

MeshThreadState.description: One thread's state in a `threadStates` reply.

state.description: Its state; absent when it does not exist.

forMessages.description: Whether any incoming message also ends the wait.

MessageId.description: A mesh message id. Unique; makes delivery idempotent at every hop.

ModeId.description: A permission / approval / sandbox mode, as the harness names it.

ModeInfo.description: A permission / approval / sandbox mode on offer.

description.description: Longer description, when the harness gives one.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the harness's default mode.

ModelCapability.description: A model-level capability with its three-valued support.

ModelId.description: A model id, exactly as the harness expects it back. Never hardcoded anywhere.

ModelInfo.description: A model, exactly as the harness listed it. Never hardcoded.

capabilities.description:
Model-level capabilities, each supported, unsupported, or unknown. A capability not
listed is unknown.

contextWindow.description: Context window in tokens, when known.

defaultEffort.description: The default effort, when the harness reports one.

efforts.description: Effort levels, in the order the harness reported them.

hidden.description: Whether the harness lists it as hidden.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the harness's default model.

about.description: The thread it concerns, when it is about another agent.

OpId.description:
A client-generated operation id. Every state-changing request carries one; re-sending
it returns the recorded outcome instead of acting again.

OriginKind.description: How a thread came to exist; drives the sidebar's "hide automated" filter.

PageCursor.description: An opaque page cursor. Bound to the snapshot that produced it.

ProjectRef.description: The repository a thread's working directory belongs to.

crossTargetKey.description:
Normalised `origin` remote URL. Two projects with the same key on different targets are
the same project. Absent: never merged across targets.

displayName.description: The repository directory name, for display.

path.description:
Identifies the project on its target: the git common directory, or the working
directory itself when there is no git.

ProjectResolveParams.description: `project/resolve`: the git identity of a directory.

commonDir.description: Git common directory (shared by all worktrees).

project.description: The project (the directory itself when there is no git).

worktree.description: The worktree; absent when there is no git.

ProtocolRange.description: The protocol versions one side speaks. Frozen core.

ProtocolVersion.description: A protocol version number. Read only by the dialect layer.

ProviderDescriptor.description: Everything the host knows about one provider instance.

capabilities.description: What this instance can do, on this backend.

harnessVersion.description: Version of the process actually serving, not just the CLI on `PATH`.

kind.description: Its kind. Display and diagnostics only — never branch on it.

modelsComplete.description:
Whether `models` is a complete listing. A model is only ever declared gone after a
complete listing.

revision.description: Bumps whenever anything above changes. Monotonic per instance.

statusMessage.description: Human-readable detail for a status other than `ready`, shown as-is.

socket.description: An explicit control socket. An instance defined by one is connect-only.

ProviderInstanceConfig.description: The stored configuration of one instance, kept on the target by `yaacd`.

implicit.description: Whether this is an implicit default instance (exists without configuration).

ProviderInstanceListResult.description: `providerInstance/list` result: the stored configurations, including implicit defaults.

instance.description: The stored configuration after the change.

ProviderInstanceUpdateParams.description:
`providerInstance/update`: a patch. Absent fields are unchanged, so an older client never
erases settings it does not know about.

endpoint.description: New endpoint: absent = unchanged, `null` = remove it.

env.description: New environment, replacing the old one entirely.

name.description: New name: absent = unchanged, `null` = remove the name.

ProviderKind.description:
A provider kind: an open string such as `codex` or `claude`. UI code must never branch on
it; branch on capabilities.

ProviderRefreshParams.description: `provider/refresh`: re-probe one instance, or all when `instance` is absent.

ProviderStatus.description:
Whether an instance can be used, and if not, why. The reasons are distinct because they
need different fixes.

provider.description: The new descriptor; its `revision` is higher than any sent before for this instance.

allowOther.description: May type a free-form answer instead.

options.description: Options; empty for a free-text question.

secret.description: The answer must be masked and never cached on the host.

QuestionAnswer.description: The answer to one question: chosen labels and/or free text.

redacted.description:
Set by `yaacd` when it reports the answer to a `secret` question: the content is
withheld, so it can never reach the host cache.

QuestionId.description: One question inside a question request.

label.description: Label; also what is sent back.

preview.description: A preview to show (markdown), when the harness offers one.

QuestionRequest.description: "Which of these approaches do you want?"

ReadThreadQuery.description: `readThread`: recent messages, or the last answer, of a thread there.

maxBytes.description: Upper bound on the reply in bytes.

ReasoningItem.description: `reasoning`: reasoning text or summary, when the provider exposes it.

reasoning.description: The text. `itemDelta` with field `reasoning` appends here.

summary.description: Whether this is a summary rather than the raw reasoning.

detail.description: Text for the agent and the user, shown as-is.

reason.description: Why it is queued or failed.

ReceiptReason.description: Why a message is queued or failed.

RequestId.description: A pending approval, question, or form inside a thread.

RequestItem.description: `request`: something awaiting the user. Journaled before anything else happens to it.

blocking.description: Whether the agent is blocked until it is answered.

answer.description: The answer, when known. Secret answers are redacted.

clientHost.description: The answering client's host name, for "answered on …".

RequestResponse.description: An answer to a request. Its `requestKind` matches the request's.

RequestState.description: The state of a request item. Always exactly one.

reachable.description: Whether the hub is connected to it now.

RpcError.description: An error response. `id` is null when the request id could not be read.

RpcId.description:
A request id. JSON-RPC allows a number or a string; YAAC sends numbers. Each side has its
own id space for the requests it originates.

RpcMessage.description: Any message. No `jsonrpc` member is sent; it is ignored if present.

RpcNotification.description: A notification: no id, no response.

RpcRequest.description: A request. `id` is unique among the sender's outstanding requests.

Seq.description: A sequence number within an epoch. Increases by one per event and is never reused.

SettingsChangedEvent.description:
`settingsChanged`: what the harness actually applied changed; carries the recomputed
effective capabilities (which include the applied settings).

effective.description: The thread's effective capabilities and applied settings, now.

SpawnThreadQuery.description: `spawnThread`: start a new thread there, as a child of the caller.

cwd.description:
Working directory on the destination. When absent, the destination resolves "the same
project" from `projectKey`; it confirms the directory exists before starting anything.

detached.description: Do not send the child's final answer back to the parent.

projectKey.description: The caller's project cross-target key (normalised remote URL).

SpawnedThread.description: One thread started by a spawn.

error.description: Why it could not be started, when it could not.

StopThreadQuery.description: `stopThread`: interrupt a thread there. Only for the caller's own workers.

StoreIdentity.description:
Which conversations an instance owns. Two instances with equal `key`s see the same
conversations; native fork is possible only within one store.

account.description: The signed-in account, as the harness reports it.

home.description: The store's home directory on the target, when it has one (Codex: `CODEX_HOME`).

key.description:
Opaque comparison key computed by `yaacd`. `None` while the store is not yet known
(for example before the first successful probe); two unknown stores are never equal.

StreamCreditParams.description:
`stream/credit` notification: the receiver of a data stream grants the sender more bytes.
Either side may send it, for a stream it receives.

bytes.description: Additional bytes the sender may send.

StreamId.description:
A data stream number, used by `0x02` data frames. Allocated by the side that will receive
the stream (for uploads: `yaacd`, in `upload/begin`).

SubscribeReplay.description: Replay: events `fromSeq ..= headSeq` follow, then live events.

fromSeq.description: First event that will be replayed.

headSeq.description: Last event in the journal now.

SubscribeReset.description: Reset: rebuild from `thread/read`, then live events strictly after its snapshot position.

headSeq.description: Last event in the journal now.

Support.description:
Three-valued support. `unknown` is a real answer — the harness gave no information —
and is never treated as "yes".

SyncToken.description: A position in `yaacd`'s thread-index change counter. Empty means "full listing".

TargetId.description: A target, as the hub identifies it: assigned when the target is added, never changed.

TargetName.description: The label the user gave a target (`devbox`). Unique, but may be renamed.

TargetPath.description:
A path on a target. Only `yaacd` on that target interprets it: the host never parses,
joins, or normalises it, and never stores it in a host `PathBuf`.

ThreadAckParams.description: `thread/ack`: how far this client has durably got. Sent periodically while attached.

seq.description: The last sequence number durably stored by the client.

ThreadEffective.description:
What a thread can do right now, computed on the target from the instance, the model, the
account, and the thread's state. The UI does not combine flags itself.

applied.description: What the harness is really using.

capabilities.description: What can be done in this thread, now.

efforts.description: Selectable now; empty when effort cannot be changed.

imageFormats.description: Accepted image media types, when known.

imageInput.description: Whether the selected model can see images. Decides `image` versus `file` parts.

ThreadEventParams.description: `thread/event` notification: one journaled event, with its position.

seq.description: The event's sequence number (the first one it covers, for a compacted `itemUpdated`).

ThreadForkParams.description: `thread/fork`: create a new thread from an existing one, with its first message.

atTurn.description:
Fork after this turn; the last completed turn when absent. A native fork honours it
only under `threadForkAtTurn`.

input.description: The first message of the new thread.

instance.description: Destination instance, on the same target.

source.description: The thread to fork from. Not modified; may be in use elsewhere.

ThreadForkPreviewParams.description:
`thread/forkPreview`: what a fork would send and where, for the confirmation dialog.
Changes nothing.

maxPreviewBytes.description: Upper bound on the transcript preview, in bytes.

cutoffTurn.description: The turn it would cut off after.

forkKind.description: The mechanism that would be used.

omittedAttachments.description: Attachments that are gone from the target and would be marked as omitted.

transcriptBytes.description: Size of the full transcript, for a handoff.

transcriptPreview.description: The beginning of the transcript, for a handoff.

unavailableReason.description: Why a fork is not possible, when it is not.

ThreadId.description:
A thread on one target. Opaque: `yaacd` builds it from the provider instance (and so its
store binding) and the harness's native conversation id. The host never parses it.

ThreadReadParams.description: `thread/read`: one page of items, newest first, from a snapshot bound to a position.

cursor.description: Continue from a previous page; absent for the first page (which takes a new snapshot).

maxBytes.description: Upper bound on the page size in bytes. Pages are bounded by bytes, never by count.

cursor.description: Cursor for the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

position.description: The journal position the snapshot is valid at. Same on every page of one snapshot.

uploads.description: Presence of the attachments referenced by the items on this page.

token.description: The index token that includes this change.

ThreadStartParams.description: `thread/start`: create a thread **and** send its first message, as one operation.

instance.description: The provider instance. Fixed for the life of the thread.

model.description: Model; the harness default when absent.

ThreadState.description: What a thread is doing, for the sidebar.

ThreadStatesQuery.description: `threadStates`: the current state of some threads there (used by `wait`).

states.description: One entry per thread asked about.

ThreadSubscribeParams.description: `thread/subscribe`: start live events for a thread, replaying from a position.

afterSeq.description: The last sequence number the client has durably applied.

epoch.description: The client's journal epoch; absent when it has no position.

activeTurn.description: The running turn, when there is one (needed for Stop and steer).

control.description: Who may act on the thread, relative to this client.

controlHolder.description: Where it is in use, for the read-only states.

effective.description: The thread's effective capabilities and applied settings.

ThreadSummary.description: What the sidebar needs, and what the host cache stores, per thread.

children.description:
How many threads this one spawned. The threads themselves are found through the
indexes (each child's `spawnedBy` names its parent, on any target).

control.description: Who may act on it, relative to the receiving client.

controlHolder.description:
Where it is in use when `control` is read-only (a host name, or a program), for
"In use on …".

forkedFrom.description: The thread whose history this one began with.

model.description: The model last applied, when known.

peers.description:
How many threads this one has exchanged messages with, without either spawning the
other.

root.description:
The orchestration root this thread belongs to, when it was spawned or messaged by an
agent.

spawnedBy.description: The agent that started this thread, possibly on another target.

title.description: Harness title, or first prompt, or user override.

maxBytes.description: Upper bound on the size of the page in bytes, chosen by the client.

token.description: The last token received; empty for a full listing.

changed.description: Summaries added or changed since the token.

full.description:
This is (the first page of) a full listing: the client replaces its cached index for
this target once the last page arrives, instead of merging.

more.description: More pages follow; call again with `token`.

removed.description: Threads the harness positively reported gone.

staleInstances.description: Instances whose last scan failed or was incomplete. Their threads stay listed.

ThreadUpdatedParams.description: `thread/updated` notification: one summary changed, pushed while connected.

token.description: The index token that includes this change.

Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, e.g. `2026-11-20T18:04:11Z`.

TokenUsage.description: Token counts. Absent counts are not reported by the harness.

input.description: The tool's input, as structured data.

output.description:
Output text. `itemDelta` with field `output` appends here. Bounded: a large output is
a head, with `outputTruncated` set.

outputBytes.description: Full output size in bytes, when known.

outputTruncated.description: The output above is a bounded head of a longer one.

ToolKind.description: What kind of tool a tool call is.

error.description: Error text, for a failed turn.

TurnId.description: A turn within a thread, as the harness identifies it.

TurnInterruptParams.description: `turn/interrupt`. Takes the turn id, so a late Stop can never hit the next turn.

TurnStartParams.description: `turn/start`: send a user message to an existing thread.

model.description: Model override (under `modelSwitch`). Sticks for later turns.

TurnSteerParams.description: `turn/steer` (under `steer`): add input to the running turn.

turnId.description: The turn the client expects to be running; `turn_mismatch` otherwise.

mediaType.description: Media type, when known (sniffed from content, not the extension).

credit.description: Initial credit in bytes on that stream. More arrives in `stream/credit`.

exists.description: The content is already stored: send no bytes and no `upload/end`.

stream.description: The data stream to send the bytes on, when `exists` is false.

UploadCancelParams.description: `upload/cancel`: abort; the daemon removes the partial file.

uploadId.description: The upload, now usable in input parts on this target.

UploadId.description: A stored upload on one target. Meaningless on any other target.

UploadPresence.description: Whether an attachment referenced by the thread is still on the target.

present.description: Whether its file still exists (temp folders can be emptied).

UploadReadParams.description: `upload/read`: a bounded read of a stored attachment (thumbnails on another host).

maxBytes.description: Upper bound on bytes returned. The daemon may return fewer.

UploadReadResult.description: `upload/read` result. Sent in the bulk class.

dataBase64.description: The bytes, standard base64 with padding.

more.description: Whether bytes remain after this read.

present.description: Whether the file is still on the target. When false, the other fields are empty.

size.description: Total size of the stored file.

tokens.description: Cumulative token usage of the thread.

parts.description: The parts. For a message sent from outside YAAC, the text as the harness stored it.

finished.description: Whether it has finished its turn (or failed, or needs attention) — what the wait is for.

WorktreeRef.description: The git worktree containing a working directory.
